main.title: Sisi pilot feedback
main.description:
Thank you for testing Sisi, a money-confidence app for young women, made with PPS Investments.

There are 18 quick questions, about 4 to 5 minutes. Every question is multiple choice, and each has an optional box if you want to say more. It is not a test of you. We are testing Sisi, and honest answers, including critical ones, help most.

What we collect: your answers here. No name, email, ID number or bank details, and no amounts of your own money. The Sisi pilot team uses them to improve the app and to report anonymised, combined results to PPS Investments.
Taking part is voluntary. You can stop at any time and skip any question you prefer not to answer.

Sisi is education, not financial advice.
main.confirmation: Thank you! Your feedback helps make Sisi better for other young women.

contact.title: Sisi pilot: stay in touch (optional)
contact.description: This is a separate form on purpose, so your contact details are never stored with your feedback answers. Only fill it in if you would like to be contacted about the pilot prize draw or future Sisi testing. Pilot reward: subject to PPS approval.
contact.confirmation: Thank you! We will only use your details for what you ticked.

main.title: Do you agree to take part?
main.purpose: Informed, voluntary, adult consent before any data is collected
main.help: You can stop at any time and skip any question you prefer not to answer.
main.source: POPIA consent; wording to be confirmed by PPS

options.v: Yes, I am 18 or older and I agree to take part

main.title: Your participant ID
main.purpose: Links this form to the anonymous in-app results without using a name or email
main.help: You will see it on the last screen of the Sisi pilot. It looks like 7K3Q. Type NONE if you did not get one.

main.title: Do you have your own account with a bank or a mobile-money service?
main.purpose: SDG 5.a baseline: access to financial services
main.source: Concept follows Global Findex account ownership; wording is ours

main.title: In the past 3 months, did you put any money aside as savings, even a small amount?
main.purpose: SDG 5.a / 4.4 baseline: saving behaviour

main.title: How much say do you usually have in big decisions about your money?
main.purpose: SDG 5.a baseline: women's say over money
main.source: Draft item for this pilot; check against a validated women's economic empowerment measure before publishing
options: I decide together with family or a partner
Other people mostly decide for me

main.title: How was your experience with each of these?
main.purpose: Experience of the six guided features, side by side (compare with what they actually did and how long each chapter took)

main.title: And the extras you peeked at, if any?
main.purpose: Experience of the features they peeked at (which to keep, fix or cut)

main.title: How easy was each of these to use or understand?
main.purpose: SDG 4.6: ease and understandability per feature, including the words and navigation
rows: Understanding my progress and weekly target
Finding my way around the app

main.title: What is Sisi mainly for?
main.purpose: SDG 4.6: did people grasp the purpose without being told? (Correct answer: the first option.)
options: Learning about money in plain words and practising with simple tools
Opening a bank account or taking out a loan
Buying and selling investments with real money

main.title: How well did Sisi speak to women like you?
main.purpose: SDG 5 / 4.5: is the content and tone gender-responsive and relevant?

main.title: What did you like? (Tick up to three)
main.purpose: Likes, in structured form
options: The short, clear lesson and quiz
That it felt private and safe

main.title: What did you dislike or find frustrating? (Tick up to three)
main.purpose: Dislikes and friction, in structured form
options: The community felt unclear or awkward
It was slow or did not work well on my phone
Data cost or a weak connection

main.title: Which ONE part of Sisi was most useful to you?
main.purpose: Forced choice: preferred feature

main.title: If we could change only ONE thing first, what should it be?
main.purpose: Forced choice: top priority to fix
options: Make the lessons shorter or simpler
Make the community easier to use
Make it faster or work better on my phone
Make it feel more like my life

main.title: Points, badges and leaderboards are optional in Sisi. How do you feel about them?
main.purpose: Gamification preference (evidence rule: must stay optional, with Focus mode)

main.title: Compared with before today, how confident do you feel about making everyday money decisions?
main.purpose: SDG 4.4 / 5.a: retrospective self-efficacy change (second estimate beside the in-app before/after)
main.source: Retrospective then/now design reduces response-shift bias

main.title: Learning about money like this could help me to… (Tick all that apply)
main.purpose: Perceived benefit by outcome area: skills (SDG 4.4) and economic agency (SDG 5.a)
options: Avoid or get out of debt
Talk about money with my family
Say no to money requests I cannot afford
Ask for fair pay or fees
Start or grow a business or side hustle
Plan for study or my career

main.title: What would make you most likely to come back? (Tick up to two)
main.purpose: Retention drivers: reminders, rewards, social, content, language, length
options: Doing it with a friend (Money Buddy)
More topics that fit my life

main.title: How safe and comfortable did you feel using Sisi, including the community?
main.purpose: SDG 5: safe participation for women online
options: I did not use the community

main.title: What could stop you using an app like Sisi regularly? (Tick all that apply)
main.purpose: SDG 5.b / 4.5: access barriers, including the gender digital divide (equity cuts for SDG 10.2)
options: Someone else controlling or checking my phone
Hard to read or tap (text size, colours, buttons)
